chunks: With his chain of narration, from Sahl, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions, who said:

I was present with Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), and Harun the Caliph, and Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya in Medina. They had come to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Harun went forward, said Salam, and stood aside. Then Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Isa ibn Ja'far went forward, said Salam, and stood with Harun. Then Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Ja'far went forward, said Salam, and stood with Harun. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) went forward and said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father! I ask Allah, who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided (people) through you, to send His blessings upon you.' Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he said?' He said, 'Yes.' Harun said, 'I testify that he is truly his father.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ: Abu al-Hasan the First (Imam Musa al-Kazim)
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَتِ: Peace be upon you, O my father

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim say to the Prophet Muhammad at his grave that impressed Harun al-Rashid?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* highlights the theological distinction between political authority and spiritual lineage, as Harun al-Rashid, the reigning Caliph, acknowledges Imam Musa al-Kazim’s superior status by accepting his greeting as proof of his true paternity. The Imam’s deliberate delay in greeting the Prophet underscores the concept of *Ihtiram* (respect) and the unique rank of the Ahl al-Bayt, who are not merely descendants but the spiritual heirs of the Prophet. This incident serves as a historical validation of the Imamate, where the Caliph himself bears witness to the Imam's divine selection and direct connection to the Prophet.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb Al-Kulayni narrated to me from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥassān, from one of our companions, who said:

I saw Abal Ḥasan the First (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)), Hārūn the (Abbasid) caliph, ‘Isā ibn Ja’far, and Ja’far ibn Yaḥyā all in Madīnah next to the grave of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.). Hārūn said to Imam Kāżim (a.s.), “Go ahead (and say Salām to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.)).” However, Imam (a.s.) refused. So Hārūn went ahead and said Salām to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and then moved aside. Then ‘Isā ibn Ja’far asked Imam (a.s.) to go ahead and say Salām to the Prophet (s.a.a.w.). However, Imam (a.s.) refused. So ‘Isā moved forward and said Salām to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and then moved aside and stood with Hārūn. Then Ja’far ibn Yaḥyā asked Imam (a.s.) to go ahead and say Salām to the Prophet (s.a.a.w.). However, Imam (a.s.) refused. So Ja’far moved forward and said Salām to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and then he also moved aside and stood with Hārūn. Then Abul Ḥasan (a.s.) moved forward and said:                Salam to you, O father! I ask Allāh who selected you, chose you, guided you, and guided (the creation) through you, to send His blessing on you. So Hārūn said to ‘Isā, “Did you hear what he said?” “Yes,” ‘Isā replied. “I testify that he (the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.)) is truly his father,” Hārūn said.
